documents.title: Rheumatology annual letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice - visit 11/18/2025

Re: Margaret Cummings

Annual SSc review. New this year: she has been more tired and more short of breath with exertion for much of 2025 - stairs at work and hills on her walks slow her down now, which was not the case a year ago. No cough. Swallowing remains a nuisance with solids but manageable. Raynaud unchanged.

Exam: sclerodactyly unchanged. Lungs clear without crackles. Heart sounds as before. No edema.

CBC and CMP normal.

Assessment: limited cutaneous SSc with new exertional dyspnea. In limited SSc this needs evaluation for pulmonary vascular disease as well as lung involvement.

Plan:
1. Complete pulmonary function tests with diffusing capacity - ordered.
2. Referral to cardiology.
3. Continue mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg BID.

Meds: mycophenolate 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Pulmonary function test report
documents.author: pulmonary function lab
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary function laboratory
Date of test: 12/09/2025
Ordering: rheumatology. Copy to primary care.

Spirometry, lung volumes and DLCO. Good effort, acceptable and reproducible.

FVC 91% predicted
FEV1 89% predicted
FEV1/FVC 0.78
TLC 93% predicted
DLCO 51% predicted

Interpretation: normal spirometry and lung volumes. Diffusing capacity moderately reduced. An isolated reduction in DLCO with preserved volumes raises the question of a pulmonary vascular process; clinical correlation advised.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - consultation 02/19/2026
Referred by rheumatology; copy to primary care.

Reason: worsening fatigue and breathlessness on exertion.

Ms. Cummings, 57, has limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis. She was seen by GI in August 2024 for chest pain and swallowing trouble and was found to have esophageal dysmotility. Over roughly the past twelve months she has become steadily more fatigued and more winded with exertion. She still has difficulty getting solid food down. Her fingers still go white and hurt in the cold, and the skin over her hands feels tight.

Medications: mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: mother rheumatoid arthritis, father hypertension, sister Hashimoto thyroiditis. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

Examination: the skin over the fingers is taut and shiny. Telangiectasias on the face. Heart: the pulmonic component of S2 is loud. Lungs clear. No edema.

Data reviewed: PFTs 12/2025 with preserved spirometry and volumes and DLCO reduced to 51% predicted. NT-proBNP today 410 pg/mL.

Assessment: progressive exertional dyspnea in limited SSc, with a loud P2 and an isolated low DLCO. Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with systemic sclerosis is suspected.

Plan:
1. Transthoracic echocardiogram.
2. Right heart catheterization through our pulmonary hypertension clinic to confirm.
3. No medication changes for now.

Cardiology

reports.text: Indication: dyspnea, suspected pulmonary hypertension in systemic sclerosis. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and systolic function; LVEF 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle mildly dilated with preserved systolic function, TAPSE 18 mm. Estimated right ventricular systolic pressure 56 mmHg. Atria normal in size. Valves structurally normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal left ventricular function, LVEF 60%. Mildly dilated right ventricle with preserved function. Estimated RVSP 56 mmHg.

documents.title: Pulmonary hypertension clinic - catheterization and treatment
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, pulmonary hypertension clinic
Visit 04/02/2026 (catheterization 03/31/2026)

Dear colleague,

Ms. Cummings underwent right heart catheterization on 3/31 via the right internal jugular vein, without complication.

Hemodynamics:
Right atrial pressure 6 mmHg
Mean pulmonary artery pressure 36 mmHg
Pulmonary artery wedge pressure 10 mmHg
Cardiac output 4.6 L/min, cardiac index 2.7 L/min/m2
Pulmonary vascular resistance 5.7 Wood units

Six-minute walk on 4/2: 405 m, lowest SpO2 94%.

Together with her echo (estimated RVSP 56 mmHg, mildly dilated RV with preserved function), NT-proBNP of 410 and the isolated low DLCO, this confirms precapillary pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with systemic sclerosis.

Plan, discussed at length with her:
1. Upfront combination therapy: ambrisentan 5 mg daily and tadalafil 20 mg daily, starting 4/2/2026. Tadalafil will go up to 40 mg daily after four weeks if tolerated. Both through a specialty pharmacy, prescribed by our clinic.
2. Continue her other medications, including mycophenolate per rheumatology.
3. Return in about 3 months with a six-minute walk and NT-proBNP.

Medications after this visit: ambrisentan 5 mg daily, tadalafil 20 mg daily, mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.

Pulmonary Hypertension Clinic

documents.title: Pulmonary hypertension clinic follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, pulmonary hypertension clinic - follow-up 06/25/2026

SSc-associated PAH, about 12 weeks into ambrisentan 5 mg daily and tadalafil, which was increased to 40 mg daily in early May. She is tolerating both. She notices she is less winded climbing hills on her walks.

Six-minute walk 440 m (405 m in April). NT-proBNP 300 pg/mL (410 in February).

Plan: continue ambrisentan 5 mg daily and tadalafil 40 mg daily. Return in 3 months.

Current medications: ambrisentan 5 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.

Pulmonary Hypertension Clinic
